title: Every way to join a word
goal: When you do not know a word's one-stroke outline, or it has none, build it from pieces you already know: hold the join key on every stroke after the first. This page lists every route.

blocks.x: Hold the join key (`+`, see [the join key](#/ref/join-key)) on every stroke after the first. Every word of two syllables or more in the dictionary can be reached at least one of these ways, most of them several. The examples are real entries. How each route is built is on [suffixes](#/ref/suffixes), [prefixes](#/ref/prefixes) and [syllables and folding](#/ref/syllables).
1. A word you know, then its ending
Stroke the stem the way you always do, then the ending's stroke.

blocks.x: Endings stack: *needlessly* is *need* `+-LS` `+-L`. A word that is two words is the two words: [[myself|PHAOEU/+SEFL]], [[outside|OUT/+SAOEUD]], and the ones speech blurs: [[noone|PHO/+WUPB]], [[nobody|PHO/+PWO*ED]], [[cannot|K/+OT]], [[everyone|EF/+WUPB]], [[anybody|AEPB/+PWO*ED]]. Both words must be common (top 5,000, and a short one top 1,000) and their consonants must add up to the word's, give or take one sound; see [syllables and folding](#/ref/syllables).
2. A prefix, then a word you know
Stroke the prefix on its own, then the word with the join key held.
When nothing above fits, say the word and stroke each syllable as you hear it.

items: **One syllable, one stroke**, with its vowel: [[table|TAEU/+PWUL]], [[machete|PHU/+SHE/+TAOE]].
**A weak last syllable drops its vowel**, exactly like a suffix: [[table|TAEU/+-BL]], [[lemon|HRE/+PH-PB]], [[profitable|PRAF/+U/+TU/+-BL]].

**A weak vowel you do stroke is `U`** (a short i is `EU`) as you hear it, **or the letter the word spells it with** as you read it: [[profitable|PRAF/+U/+TU/+-BL]] and [[profitable|PRAF/+O/+TO/+-BL]].

**Split anywhere you hear a break**: [[lemon|HREPL/+UPB]] (*lem-on*) and [[lemon|HRE/+PHUPB]] (*le-mon*) both work, and so do *com-pro-mise* [[compromise|KOPL/+PRO/+PHAOEUZ]], *comp-ro-mise* [[compromise|KOPL/+PR/+PHAOEUZ]] and *compro-mise* [[compromise|KOPL/+PROPL/+AOEUZ]]. Any run of consonants that can start a syllable may go to the next stroke, or none.
**Hold the join key on every stroke after the first**, always: `KOPL/+PRO/+PHAOEUZ`. Without it each stroke is a word of its own (*column*, *prah*, *meyez*), which is the whole point of the key.
**A weak last syllable that fits on the stroke before it can fold onto it**: [[sensible|SEPB/+SU/+-BL]] or [[sensible|SEPB/+SUBL]].

**Any run of sounds is a stroke.** Three, four, five and six strokes work too: [[complete|KU/+PH/+HRAOET]], [[complete|K/+UPL/+PHRAOET]], [[complete|KU/+-PL/+-P/+HRAOET]]. The cheapest of each length are in the dictionary (24 / 24 / 12 / 6 / 3 for two to six strokes). `lyk paths complete` lists every way and which are in. Every word with a pronunciation gets these, whether or not it has a primary yet when the joins are placed.

**Or spell it the way it looks.** Every word is also held the way its letters read, a syllable at a time, even where the dictionary hears something else: [[contemplation|KOPB/+TEPL/+PHRAEU/+SHUPB]] (*con* with an o, *tem* with an e), [[hour|H/+O/+UR]]. Each vowel letter may be short (`A`), long (`AEU`) or weak (`U`); *c*, *g* and *s* may be hard or soft; a silent e is optional at the end (*table*) and between a vowel-consonant and the next consonant ([[movement|PHOF/+PHEPBT]], *hope* + *ful*). If you can read the word's syllables, you can type them.

**A shorter word, then the rest spelled out.** Any start of the word that is a word with a one-stroke outline of its own can be struck as that word, with the rest after it spelled the same way, from one stroke up: [[movement|PHOF/+PHEPBT]] (*move*, then *ment*), [[particular|PART/+EUBG/+UL/+AR]] (*part*, *ic*, *ul*, *ar*). Up to 3 / 4 / 4 / 2 ways for the rest in one, two, three, four strokes (`REST_QUOTAS`).

**A word that sounds like a commoner one takes that one's paths and the star** when it has no joins of its own. *ok* sounds like *okay*: [[ok|O/+KAEU/+*]], the same path with the star marker stroke after it, the way a name takes its sound-alike's stroke ([[matt|PHAT/+*]]). So are *principle* and *dessert*. The marked ones never count as a spare outline when the phrase pass decides whether a word can lose its stroke to a phrase (*ar* keeps `AR`).

blocks.x: Most long words also have a one-stroke short form (see [how short](#/ref/brevity)): [[profitable|PROFBLT]], [[machete|PHEFPT]]. Learn those for the words you type often. The joins above are there for every other word.
